intro: PDF to WEBP turns each page of a PDF into a WEBP image, the format websites use to load quickly. At the same visual quality it is usually smaller than JPG, so it is a good choice for showing pages of a catalogue, a menu or a brochure on a website or online shop.

Pages are drawn in your browser with PDFium and never leave your device; batches too large for the browser are processed on the server with the same engine. Adjust the quality between 1 and 100 % (85 by default) to balance sharpness and size, and the resolution between 72 and 600 DPI: 144 is enough for screens and higher values let you zoom in without losing detail.

Choose colour or greyscale and which pages you want, all of them or ranges such as “2-5, 8”. In the additional options you can ask for a single long image with all pages stacked, practical for showing a complete document with vertical scrolling.

Images carry the name of the PDF and the page number; when there is more than one, they are downloaded together in a ZIP, with one folder per document if you convert several PDFs. If a file has a password, you will be asked for it to open the file, and each page has a pixel limit so your device does not run out of memory.

faq.a: Current browsers display it without trouble; some older editing or office programs may not support it, in which case PDF to JPG is a better fit.
The default 85 % balances sharpness and size; raise it if the document has small print or lower it if you need lighter files.

faq.q: What about converting WEBP to PDF?
faq.a: Use WEBP to PDF, which gathers WEBP images into a document.
